close_reason: Resolved 2026-05-10: percent_encode now returns Cow<'_, str>. Common JMAP IDs (alphanumeric + unreserved chars) return Cow::Borrowed with zero allocation. Only inputs needing escape allocate via Cow::Owned. The other half (url_scheme) was already fixed in JMAP-6lsm.10 — current implementation returns Option<&str> with eq_ignore_ascii_case comparison. 4 new oracle-backed unit tests cover both Cow variants and uppercase-hex encoding (RFC 3986 §2.1). cargo test --workspace clean; cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean. Commit 2959118.
description:
Two micro-allocation findings in crate-jmap-base-client:

1. `url_scheme` (client.rs:629) calls `to_ascii_lowercase()` allocating a fresh String per call only to compare to literals "http"/"https". `eq_ignore_ascii_case` on the prefix slice would be allocation-free. Called once per JMAP request.

2. `percent_encode` (blob.rs:129) always allocates even when the input has no chars needing escape. A `Cow<'_, str>` return would let the safe-input path skip allocation.

Why both opinion: micro-opts. No measured perf impact. Fine as-is.

jmap-base-client is the foundation client crate per workspace AGENTS.md. Listed for completeness.
title: P3: percent_encode and url_scheme allocate unnecessarily
